about.heading: How we work
body: Empire Granit produces granite monuments, borders, engraving, installation, and cemetery plot work. A project usually starts in the Narva office or from photos and dimensions sent remotely.

Before production we clarify the plot condition, shape, stone, inscription, portrait, additional elements, and installation. That gives the family a clear scope and a clear reason for the final price.
Communication stays practical: consultation is available in Russian, Estonian, and English by phone, email, WhatsApp, or form, and agreed details are confirmed before work starts.
about.title: Workshop and contact point in Narva
about.lead: We help families choose and order a granite monument that fits the plot, budget, and future care needs. The focus is clear consultation, careful production, and calm installation.
points: An order starts with dimensions, inscription text, granite choice, and a practical price range.
Material, engraving, portrait, border, transport, and installation are discussed as separate parts.
When needed, a photo of the old monument or plot helps us explain what can be restored or added.

privacy.heading: Privacy Policy

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: Callback form: name and phone number. Inquiry form: name, email, and message text. Both forms also record the chosen site language and the form type. We do not request other personal data.

sections.title: Where your data goes
sections.body: Form submissions are delivered to our team through Formspree (formspree.io), a third-party processor that forwards messages to us. Anonymous usage events (page views, form submissions) are stored in Google Firebase (Firestore) so we can improve the site. Traffic statistics are measured with Plausible Analytics, which is cookieless and collects no personal identifiers.

sections.title: Why we use it
sections.body: Solely to reply to your request, prepare a proposal, agree on installation, and improve the website. We do not run advertising profiles and do not sell data to third parties.

sections.title: Retention
sections.body: Form submissions and analytics events are kept for 12 months and then deleted, unless an active order or legal obligation requires longer storage.

sections.title: Your rights and contact

faq.heading: FAQ
faq.intro: Practical answers before ordering a monument, installation, engraving, or site work.
faq.contactCta: Did not find your answer? Get an estimate

items.question: When can a monument be installed after a funeral?
items.answer: Timing depends on cemetery rules, ground condition, and season. Often families wait for ground settlement; exact timing should be checked for the specific site.

items.question: How long does production take?
items.answer: Usually 2 to 6 weeks, depending on material, shape complexity, engraving, portrait, and seasonal workload.

items.question: What affects the price?
items.answer: Size, thickness and color of granite, shape complexity, engraving, portrait, border, foundation preparation, distance, and cemetery conditions.

items.question: What is included in installation?
items.answer: Scope depends on the order. We usually discuss site preparation, foundation, product installation, and any extra work needed.

items.question: Can I order remotely?
items.answer: Yes. Send site photos, dimensions, wishes, inscription text, and portrait photo. Details can be agreed by phone or in writing.

items.question: Which materials should I choose?
items.answer: Granite is commonly chosen for monuments because it is durable and calm in appearance. Color, thickness, and texture are selected by budget, style, and site.

items.question: Are cemetery permits needed?
items.answer: Some cemeteries have rules for installation, dimensions, and work timing. We can help clarify what is needed for the specific location.

items.question: Do you work across Estonia?
items.answer: Yes, orders, delivery, and installation are possible across Estonia by agreement. Conditions depend on distance and access.

items.question: Can an old monument be restored?
items.answer: Yes. Cleaning, lettering renewal, portrait renewal, individual elements, and general appearance can often be improved. First we assess the condition by photo or on site.

items.question: Is there a guarantee for installation or work?
items.answer: We are responsible for the agreed scope and explain conditions before the order starts. Specific terms depend on work type, material, and foundation condition.

items.question: How should a monument be maintained?
items.answer: Use gentle cleaning without aggressive chemicals. For lettering, portrait, or site covering renewal, ask for separate guidance.

items.question: How do I send a photo or inscription for engraving?
items.answer: Send the photo and text through the form, email, or messenger. Before production we approve spelling, font, and placement.

process.heading: How a family memorial is created
process.intro: We guide the family through each step calmly: first consultation, design direction, clear price, production, and installation.
process.ctaBody: Send a photo of the plot, preferred dimensions, or a simple question. We will explain what to clarify next and which solution is realistic.

steps.title: First conversation
paragraphs: We begin by phone, email, or at the workshop with a calm conversation. We clarify who the memorial is for, which cemetery the plot is in, and whether the work needs to be ready for a specific date.

The family can bring a plot photo, cemetery rules, measurements of an existing memorial, or simply a list of wishes. If there is little information, we help ask the right questions and collect missing details in order.
By the end of this step, the starting point is clear: plot type, work scope, timing, and the next decision the family needs to make.

steps.title: Design direction
paragraphs: Together we review the monument shape, granite color, engraving layout, portrait, symbols, and whether a border is needed. The goal is not speed, but a dignified proportion and material that fits the cemetery setting.

The family can bring reference photos, an old design, inscription text, birth and death dates, and notes about a portrait or photo enamel. When useful, we suggest several realistic directions with different budgets and work scopes.
The result is a chosen design direction with the main materials, inscription, and added details listed clearly.

steps.title: Clear agreement
paragraphs: Once the direction is chosen, we set out the work scope, price, payment terms, and expected schedule. Installation, removal of an old stone, plot preparation, and extra work are listed separately.
The family confirms names, dates, engraving text, dimensions, and selected materials. We check this part carefully because changes are limited after production begins.
By the end, the family has a clear agreement: what will be made, when the next step starts, and the final price.

steps.title: Careful production
paragraphs: In the workshop we produce the stone, engraving, and additional details according to the approved solution. We check dimensions, edge finish, text readability, and how each detail works as part of the whole.
If something needs confirmation before final finishing, we send the necessary view or clarification. For portraits, photo enamel, or complex engraving, review points are agreed separately.
The result is a memorial ready for installation with the agreed details completed.

steps.title: Installation and photo
paragraphs: On installation day we prepare the place, set the base, install the memorial, and check alignment and stability. If agreed, we also finish the surface, border, or nearby area.
The family does not always need to be present. If agreed, we send a photo of the completed work and note whether anything at the cemetery should be maintained later.
Finally, the family receives a finished plot and clear information about care, cleaning, and possible future additions.
